task_name: The plugin's groom, driven by this backend
summary: CtGroomEpic drives ct-groom.mjs: planned() runs it with --dry-run and parses stdout into a GroomPlan (milestone + one GroomPlanIssue per issue, projecting only order/title/labels), run() runs it for real; both treat exit 0 and 3 as success and raise EpicNotGroomed for anything else, with the exception's message set to said.stderr.trim() verbatim (byte for byte, no wrapping prose) so the cabin can show the plugin's own words untranslated. Malformed stdout under --dry-run raises GroomPlanNotUnderstood. Added the EpicGroomFailure family (EpicNotGroomed, GroomPlanNotUnderstood) to domain/exceptions.ts, wired both leaves into start-plan-route.ts's shared PlanCollapse table (codes epic-not-groomed / groom-plan-not-understood), and added EpicGroomFailure to plan-refusal.test.ts's FAMILIES so the family root itself isn't expected to carry its own refusal. Verified the exit-code branch and the verbatim-message assertion by hand-mutation (both caught, file restored identical). npm --prefix backend run typecheck and the full backend suite (80 files, 1709 tests) are green.

Parented PublishedSpecNotRead under the existing SpecFreezeFailure family rather than a new one, so plan-refusal.test.ts's FAMILIES list (out of this task's Files line) needed no change; ran it and refusal-codes.test.ts plus the full backend suite (1722 tests) to confirm no regression. The epic's issues on GitHub, read and promoted
summary: GhEpicIssues.listOf runs `gh issue list --milestone <m> --state all --json number,url,title,labels,state`, projects only number/url/title/labels[].name/state (rejecting any issue that doesn't read as that shape), derives each EpicIssue's status with the plugin's own resolveStatus (no second opinion, D-11), and sorts ascending by number; promote() runs `gh issue edit --add-label status:ready --remove-label status:backlog` via the shared GhPlanIssues.READY_LABEL/BACKLOG_LABEL constants so the vocabulary stays declared once (BACKLOG_LABEL added to GhPlanIssues joining the existing three). The fixture in gh-epic-issues.test.ts is a real capture: `gh issue list --repo mercadona/control-tower --milestone "start-in-correct-loop" --state all --limit 200 --json number,url,title,labels,state`, run 2026-09-15, keeping issues #329/#330 verbatim (labels, ids and colors included) so the parse is proved against gh's real shape; provenance is named as the describe() block title, following the ct-groom-epic.test.ts/gh-published-specs.test.ts precedent. Amendment: added `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/plan-refusal.test.ts` (modify) to Task 3's Files: line in the plan, because introducing the new EpicIssuesFailure family (housing EpicIssuesNotRead/EpicIssuesNotUnderstood/EpicIssueNotPromoted, per domain.md's two-cause-family rule) makes that pre-existing test enumerate EpicIssuesFailure itself as a 'way the plan can collapse' needing its own PlanCollapse entry; the fix is registering it in that test's FAMILIES whitelist, exactly the pattern task 1 already used for EpicGroomFailure (and task 1's own plan already declared that same file for that same reason, so this is filling a gap task 3's plan text left out). Mutation sweep (each introduced by hand on a clean tree, run against gh-epic-issues.test.ts, confirmed red, then restored and diffed identical to the original): flipping isPromotable's && to || caught; dropping listOf's final .sort() caught; swapping promoteArgvFor's add/remove labels caught; inverting the isOpen === GhEpicIssues.OPEN comparison caught; stubbing resolveStatus's result caught. Two survived and were repaired by strengthening (not renaming) the existing 'a gh that failed raises...' test: bypassing the `!Array.isArray(parsed) || !parsed.every(#readsAsAnIssue)` shape check entirely left the suite green until I added a wrong-shape-object case and a malformed-single-issue case (numeric `state`), both now asserted as EpicIssuesNotUnderstood. One mutation was left deliberately unrepaired and is declared rather than fixed: gutting EpicIssue's own constructor guards (number/url/title/status non-empty) also leaves the suite green, because GhEpicIssues only ever constructs it from already-validated raw JSON; this matches the codebase's existing precedent (PlanIssue, RepositoryName, FreezeFinding) of never unit-testing a value object's own shape guard directly — it is an invariant the type defends for itself, not a use case's observable behaviour. Verification: npm --prefix backend run typecheck (exit 0), npm --prefix backend test -- __tests__/infrastructure/gh-epic-issues.test.ts __tests__/infrastructure/gh-plan-issues.test.ts (52 tests, exit 0), the status:ready grep check (exit 0), and the full backend suite (82 files, 1739 tests, exit 0).

Gate 2's state, derived from evidence
summary: Added ReadEpicGroom, the ladder query for gate 2's state (no-spec, draft, awaiting-publication, groomable, groomed, authorised), asking EpicSpecs, PublishedSpecs, EpicIssues and EpicGroom in that order and short-circuiting before each unneeded collaborator; the dry run (EpicGroom#planned) is asked only at groomable, verified both by the six unit tests (doubles' recorded `asked` arrays) and by the plan's grep-for-'planned' check. Used the non-null assertion spec.title()! at the point where a frozen, published spec's title becomes the milestone name, mirroring the existing spec.frozenOn()! precedent in freeze-spec.ts, since EpicSpecs.mostRecent()'s real adapter (DiskEpicSpecs) already guarantees a non-null title before returning a spec — the port's own type does not encode that invariant, so a future adapter that violated it would surface as a runtime TypeError here rather than a compile error. Verified two of the ladder's branch decisions (awaiting-publication vs falling through, and groomed vs authorised) by hand-mutating the production file, confirming the corresponding test failed for the stated reason, then restoring the file byte-for-byte before finishing. typecheck and the new test file both pass; no other files touched.

Gate 2's press: the promotion
summary: Added PromoteEpic, which asks ReadEpicGroom once, refuses (no second read, no promote call) when the milestone holds no issue at all, otherwise calls EpicIssues.promote once per issue answering isPromotable() in listed order, then reads again and answers the milestone's real state, issues and the promoted numbers. The four tests cover: exactly the promotable issues (an explicit backlog one and one whose title documents that a missing status: label resolves to backlog, per GhEpicIssues' use of the plugin's resolveStatus) are asked of the EpicIssues double while the in-progress and closed-backlog ones are not; a refused epic with no issue never calls promote; an already-authorised epic promotes nothing without failing; and the answer's issues come from the second read, not the first. Mutation sweep by hand (filter forced true, refusal check forced false, answer built from `before` instead of `after`, `promoted` built from `before.issues` instead of `waiting`) killed all four mutants, each with the test whose name names that behaviour, then the file was restored and verified identical. typecheck and the task's own test file both pass; the file contains exactly one `isPromotable` occurrence as the verification script requires.
